idiom_name: visitor struct of function pointers with a NULL slot for each element it cannot visit
implementation_notes: C has no inheritance, multiple interface implementation or runtime type information, so the role structure is hand-written: forward-declare each element, define a Visitor struct with one function pointer per concrete element, and embed an acceptor header as the first member of every element struct. A concrete visitor leaves unsupported slots NULL and each element's accept tests its own slot before calling it; that NULL check is the manual analogue of the failed cross cast and makes partial visitation explicit. This is not type-checked acyclic Visitor, so keep the callback table and layout conventions local and documented. Use a fully populated visitor struct (all slots set, no tests) only when every operation must handle every element.
pitfalls: The visitor struct must be zero-initialised before the handled slots are assigned; an uninitialised function pointer is invoked as if it were a handler instead of failing the test, which is undefined behaviour rather than a skipped visit.

accept must be reached through the element's own acceptor header; casting an element pointer to the wrong struct type silently reinterprets the layout, so keep the header first and never hand out the payload pointer as the element.
Without a slot test or a kind tag there is no representation of the visitor cannot visit this element outcome, so a partial visitor crashes instead of being skipped.
